candidates.title: Disable st.data_editor by cell (and row): cell/row-level editability
candidates.text:
### Summary

**Current Behavior**: Only full columns of an `st.data_editor` can be enabled or disabled for user-editing.

**Feature Request**: Allow for assigning editability on cell (and row) level. For example, an editable column should be disabled for cells (rows) where a certain condition is met.

**Workaround**: Currently, there is no functional workaround. I tried to implement a customized handling of the user input to catch undesired edits and raise an exception when a user edits a cell that should not be editable (in a non-disabled column). However the session_state (e.g. `st.session_state[<data_editor_key>]["edited_rows"].items()`)of the `st.data_editor` does not allow for manipulating the user-input, so the user has to manually undo their changes or refresh the streamlit page and (potentially) re-enter all other edits (in case of bulk edits).

candidates.title: Selectbox dropdown renders behind st.dialog (options hidden, mouse clicks don't register)
candidates.text:
### Expected Behavior

The dropdown option list appears on top of the dialog, and clicking an option selects it (as it does for a selectbox outside a dialog).

candidates.title: Widgets in an st.popover opened inside an st.dialog are occluded by the dialog and unusable
candidates.text:
### Expected Behavior

The popover body renders above the dialog and its widgets are fully interactive:
opening the `selectbox`, picking an option, and having the value commit —
dismissing neither the popover nor the dialog. (This is how it behaved in 1.58.0.)

candidates.title: file_uploader API docstrings 1.49.0
candidates.text:
on_change : callable
    An optional callback invoked when this file_uploader's value
    changes.

args : list or tuple
    An optional list or tuple of args to pass to the callback.

kwargs : dict
    An optional dict of kwargs to pass to the callback.

disabled : bool
    An optional boolean that disables the file uploader if set to
    ``True``. The default is ``False``.

label_visibility : "visible", "hidden", or "collapsed"
    The visibility of the label. The default is ``"visible"``. If this
    is ``"hidden"``, Streamlit displays an empty spacer instead of the
    label, which can help keep the widget aligned with other widgets.
    If this is ``"collapsed"``, Streamlit displays no label or spacer.

width : "stretch" or int
    The width of the file uploader widget. This can be one of the
    following:

    - ``"stretch"`` (default): The width of the widget matches the
      width of the parent container.
    - An integer specifying the width in pixels: The widget has a
      fixed width. If the specified width is greater than the width of
      the parent container, the width of the widget matches the width
      of the parent container.

candidates.title: Selectbox dropdown renders behind st.dialog (options hidden, mouse clicks don't register)
candidates.text:
### Summary

When an `st.selectbox` is placed inside an `st.dialog`, opening its dropdown renders the option list **behind** the dialog. The options are visually hidden and mouse clicks fall through to the widgets stacked on top, so the selection never changes. Keyboard selection (↓ + Enter) still works, which is the giveaway that the options exist but are not reachable by mouse.

candidates.title: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list
candidates.section: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list > Additional Context
candidates.text:
### Additional Context

This feature request was inspired by a common use case discussed while using st.date_input  with dataframes. The current workaround is to use st.selectbox with the list of available dates, but this sacrifices the calendar UI   experience.

Related issue: st.date_input currently supports min_value and max_value for continuous 
ranges, but has no support for non-continuous date lists.

candidates.title: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG
candidates.text:
### How?

Keep the existing native download icon on Altair/Vega-Lite (and other Vega) charts, in the same toolbar row as Fullscreen.

When the pointer hovers that download icon, show a compact dropdown that matches the toolbar (same icon size, radius, colors, light/dark theme). Suggested items:

- Download PNG
- Download SVG

Clicking an item exports from the current Vega view (`toImageURL("png")` / `toImageURL("svg")`) and starts a browser download.

A click with no menu selection can keep today's PNG-only behavior as the default.

I do not need a new `st` command. Optional later: `st.altair_chart(..., download_formats=("png", "svg"))` to choose which items appear. A Python API is nice-to-have; the hover menu on the native icon is the main request.

Please do not bring back the old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu (View Source / Open in Vega Editor). This should stay a Streamlit toolbar control.
